commitResults.messageTitle: added task class to new file
Extract user interaction into Ui class
commitResults.messageBody: Move standard input handling and user-facing output from Bob into Ui. Route greetings, commands, task responses, and errors through the new collaborator while preserving existing behavior. This establishes a focused boundary for future Parser, TaskList, and Storage extractions.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract command parsing into Parser class
commitResults.messageBody: Move command keyword recognition out of Bob and into Parser. Bob now delegates command classification while retaining all existing command handling and user-facing behavior. This creates a focused boundary for the remaining command parsing and task-list extractions.

Introduce TaskList as the owner of in-memory tasks, including add, remove, lookup, sizing, validation, and persistence-copy operations. Update Bob handlers to use TaskList while preserving command behavior and storage format.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract file persistence into Storage class
commitResults.messageBody: Replace the static TaskStorage utility with an instance-based Storage collaborator configured by Bob. Add Bob construction and run lifecycle while preserving task file format and command behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Make tasklist methods adhere to OOP principles
Add test cases for Parser and TaskList
Change to adhere to coding standard

commitResults.messageBody:
Task data and event dates rely on non-null values and valid relationships,
but these assumptions are implicit in the code.

Undetected violations can cause methods to fail or behave unexpectedly.

Let's add assertions in Parser, Task, TaskList, Deadline, Event, and
Storage to document these assumptions.

Assertions make programmer errors easier to diagnose while keeping normal
user-input validation handled by exceptions.

Assertions must be enabled during development and testing.

The execute method mixes command dispatch with argument parsing, task mutation, persistence, and response formatting. Its length and multiple abstraction levels make the main command flow harder to read and increase the cost of changing one command without affecting others.

Extract command-specific handlers and shared task-list formatting so execute now serves as a concise dispatcher. Preserve the existing public API, response text, persistence behavior, and exception behavior while making each responsibility easier to understand and test independently.

The parseTask method combines record validation, task-type dispatch, date parsing, and completion-state restoration. Its length and nested branches make the file format rules harder to understand and maintain.

Extract the deadline and event parsers, and isolate completion restoration behind named helpers. Keep malformed records ignored and preserve the existing task construction and completion behavior while making each parsing responsibility explicit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Place GUI classes in bob package
commitResults.messageBody:
The GUI classes use the default package while the application classes use the named bob package. This inconsistency weakens namespace organization and makes the application entry point and FXML controller harder to locate.

Move the GUI classes into bob and update the Gradle entry point and FXML controller reference. Keep the runtime wiring unchanged while making package ownership explicit and consistent.

Public GUI factory methods and the controller injection method lack documentation describing their parameters and results. This forces callers to infer their behavior from implementation details.

Add concise Javadoc with parameter and return descriptions so the public GUI API communicates its purpose consistently with the rest of the project.

TaskList uses unexplained numeric substring offsets when removing command keywords. These magic numbers make command parsing harder to verify and can become incorrect when command syntax changes.

Replace the offsets with named constants so each extraction documents which command prefix it removes. Preserve all command parsing behavior while making the intent explicit.

addDeadline performs syntax validation, field extraction, date parsing, and task creation in one method. The combined responsibilities make the normal creation path less prominent and obscure the validation rules.

Move deadline syntax and field validation into a named helper. Keep the same errors and task creation behavior while making addDeadline focus on constructing the task.

addEvent performs syntax validation, field extraction, date parsing, and task creation in one method. The combined responsibilities make the normal creation path less prominent and obscure the validation rules.

Move event syntax and field validation into a named helper. Keep the same errors and task creation behavior while making addEvent focus on constructing the task.

Several fields are assigned once and never reassigned after construction. Leaving them mutable suggests that later reassignment is part of the design and makes object state harder to reason about.

Declare stable Storage, Parser, and GUI Bob references as final. Preserve initialization behavior while communicating the intended immutability of these dependencies.

TaskList and Storage expose ArrayList in several method signatures even though callers only need list operations. Concrete collection types couple the components unnecessarily and make future collection changes more disruptive.

Use List for task collection fields, constructors, and persistence boundaries while retaining ArrayList for local construction and defensive copies. Preserve ordering and indexing behavior while depending on the smallest useful abstraction.

Task serialization repeats unexplained type and completion literals across the task classes and storage parser. The repeated protocol values make the file format harder to understand and change consistently.

Centralize the task type and completion markers as named constants and reuse them in serialization and parsing. Preserve the storage format while making the protocol meanings explicit.
